$comment: Locales allowed to be missing English keys, and why (SC-409).
A locale NOT named here must answer every key in en.json — that is the
guard in tests/lib/i18n-locales.test.ts, and it exists because i18next
resolves a missing key to the English string and renders it. Russian was
50 keys behind within hours of shipping complete, and nothing failed.
Naming a locale here exempts it from COMPLETENESS only. Every structural
check still applies: it must exist on both sides of the split, name itself
in $meta, have a row in LANGUAGE_FORMATS, and carry every plural form its
language has for the keys it does define.
This is a file someone edits deliberately, not a threshold. Adding a line
is a reviewable act that says 'this language is knowingly partial'. The
test also fails when a named locale has CAUGHT UP, so the exemption cannot
Trade-off, stated rather than hidden: a locale named here can drift
further with nothing failing. That is strictly better than the defect this
replaces, where a locale believed COMPLETE drifted with nothing failing —
